attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No theorem yet converts SAT-semantic, nonrelativizing certificates into functional certificates or into charged row-selection transcripts. That is the exact remaining gap, not a proof of P != NP.
steps: Instantiate the surviving carrier with L=(log N)^d, d>1, T_N=N^q, q<1+epsilon, and generator size N^rho with rho<1+epsilon.
Assume a certificate predicate P_N is dense, 2^{O(L)}-constructive, and functionally sound for every label vector ell. Define R_L(f)=1 iff exists pi P_N(ell_f,pi).
Constructivity of R_L is polynomial in the truth-table length 2^L, and density is at least 2^{-O(L)}, so R_L is large in the Razborov-Rudich sense.

If f has circuits of size L^c, substituting f into the XOR generator gives C(H_{N,f})<=N^{max{q,rho}+o(1)}<N^{1+epsilon}; functional soundness therefore forces R_L(f)=0. This proves usefulness against L^c circuits for every fixed c.

If P_N is not functional, extract the charged row-selection transcript it uses. A transcript with A_N+S_N+min{R_N,K_NC(SAT_L)}+E_NN below N^{1+epsilon} is a concrete falsifier of the claimed source lower-bound route.

Validity regime check: the derivation uses the definitions and assumptions listed in the candidate lemmas, preserves the same source object and target object, and is valid only in the stated P vs NP branch model with its declared circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity conditions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a route-level no-go and validation filter. It only says which beta=0 XOR certificate styles naturalize or leak advice; it does not prove the required N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for H_N^{SAT}.

assumptions: Model is nonuniform fan-in two Boolean circuits; all advice, certificate, generator, and decoder costs are charged in the stated size bounds.
Uniformity regime: G_N and the verifier for P_N are constructible from 1^N in poly(N) or are explicitly charged as N^rho and 2^{O(L)} objects.
Functional soundness regime: acceptance of P_N(ell,pi) is a theorem about H_{N,ell} for arbitrary label vectors, not only about the real SAT label vector.
Largeness regime: A_N={ell: exists pi P_N(ell,pi)} has density at least 2^{-aL} among all 2^{2^L} L-bit truth tables for some fixed a.
Same-theory condition: usefulness is against the same nonuniform circuit class used in the substitution upper bound; no oracle, algebraic extension, or hidden advice is allowed.
definitions: source object: H_{N,ell}(x)=\oplus_{j\le T_N} ell(G_N(x,j)), where x has length N, T_N=N^q, G_N has circuit size N^rho, and G_N outputs L=(log N)^d bit target instances.
target object: the truth-table label vector ell_f of an L-bit Boolean function f; the intended target is ell_{SAT_L} on encoded formulas of length L.
controlled interface: substitute a target circuit for f into each generated query, and verify/search P_N(ell,pi) in 2^{O(L)} time without label-dependent row advice.
target-preserving condition: max{q,rho}<1+epsilon, d>1 fixed, beta=0 since L=N^{o(1)}, and P_N(ell,pi) soundly implies C(H_{N,ell})>N^{1+epsilon} for every label vector ell.

Thus a dense proof-mediated source lower bound escapes the natural-proofs obstruction only by being nonfunctional, nonlarge, nonconstructive, advice-leaking, or SAT-semantic and explicitly nonrelativizing.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing theorem is direct cluster soundness or a consistency extractor for the specific lower-bound verifier; ordinary proof soundness does not imply it.
steps: Encode each row r in C_m as a relation R_r(y|Q_r,z|I_r) over target bits and proof-view variables.
Define P_m(y)=1 iff the CSP over rows C_m is satisfiable for the fixed target table y.
Completeness gives one satisfying proof-view assignment for TT(SAT_m); therefore all truth tables agreeing with TT(SAT_m) on the h_m queried target coordinates also lie in P_m.
A hypertree-decomposition dynamic program decides the existential proof-view CSP in time (N|C_m|)^{O(1)}2^{O(tau_m v_m)}, which is poly(N) under tau_m v_m=O(log N).
Direct cluster soundness implies no truth table of a size m^k circuit lies in P_m, so P_m is useful against the named target class.
Thus any such cluster yields a valid large constructive useful property; under same-class PRF security, the route faces natural-proofs pressure rather than escaping via long proofs.
Tested replacement of direct soundness by ordinary soundness and found a blocking falsifier: inconsistent cycle-XOR systems have globally no proof but locally satisfiable bounded-width shadows.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a conditional naturalization/no-go gate for one route family, not a proof of P != NP. High-width, nonexplicit, nonlarge, or genuinely semantic proof-system-specific certificates may still escape, but they now owe named transfer certificates.

assumptions: Model: nonuniform Boolean circuits SIZE_m(m^k) over m input bits; the lower-bound statement is slice-wise and truth-table based.
Uniformity: V_m and C_m are generated in poly(N) time, with no hidden superpolynomial advice selecting the cluster.
Completeness: TT(SAT_m) has a proof assignment satisfying every row in C_m.
Width regime: |C_m|<=N^a and tau_m*v_m<=b log N for constants a,b independent of m.
Naturalness regime: h_m<=c log N, so the accepting cylinder around TT(SAT_m) has polynomial density.
Soundness regime: usefulness is not inferred from ordinary global proof soundness; it is the direct cluster soundness stated above.
definitions: source object: a uniform proof-mediated local verifier V_m for the lower-bound statement LB_m = CC(TT(SAT_m))>m^k, with row r reading target coordinates Q_r and proof coordinates I_r.

target object: the total truth-table property P_m subseteq {0,1}^N defined by P_m(y)=1 iff there exists an assignment to the proof cells touched by C_m satisfying every row predicate in the explicit cluster C_m.
controlled interface: an explicit row cluster C_m with h_m=|union_{r in C_m} Q_r| target-table queries, proof view size v_m=max_r |I_r|, and proof-view hypergraph H_m={I_r:r in C_m}.

target-preserving condition: direct cluster soundness holds, meaning for every m-input circuit A of size at most m^k and every assignment to the touched proof cells, at least one row in C_m rejects TT(A).
N=2^m is the truth-table length; constructivity means P_m is decidable in poly(N) time uniformly from m.
tau_m denotes generalized hypertree width of H_m; acyclic view clusters are the special case tau_m=1.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-level no-go bridge: it turns a structurally tame long-proof lower-bound certificate into a large constructive useful property, hence into a valid natural-proofs conflict under same-class PRF hardness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Bounded-width proof-view clusters do not constitute a long-proof escape. If a proof-mediated local verifier for CC(TT(SAT_m))>m^k has an explicit row cluster whose target-query union is O(log N), whose proof-view hypergraph has generalized hypertree width tau with tau*v=O(log N), and whose cluster is directly sound against every SIZE_m(m^k) truth table, then the induced existential cluster shadow is a valid Razborov-Rudich natural property useful against SIZE_m(m^k).

assumptions: The falsifier is finite and structural; it attacks the bridge from local consistency to usefulness, not the P versus NP conjecture.
Rows may be encoded as 3-XOR constraints with constant proof-view size after standard arity reduction.
The target bits can be ignored or fixed in the falsifier, showing the obstruction lies in proof consistency rather than SAT semantics.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: a proof-view CSP extracted from verifier rows, with proof variables as CSP variables and row predicates as local constraints.
target object: the induced existential shadow P_C(y) obtained by asking whether the row constraints in C have some proof-view assignment.
controlled interface: replacement of direct cluster soundness by the weaker assertion that no single global proof satisfies all verifier rows.

target-preserving condition: a cluster proves circuit lower bounds only if satisfiability of its local CSP is impossible for every small-circuit truth table, not merely impossible globally for one inconsistent proof instance.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Ordinary proof soundness cannot be substituted for direct cluster soundness. A cyclic XOR or 3-XOR consistency system can be globally unsatisfiable while every acyclic or low-width subcluster is satisfiable, so bounded-width local shadows may be large and constructive but not useful against the target class.

A proof-view hypergraph with tau_m v_m=omega(log N) can make CSP recognition superpolynomial in N, defeating constructivity without proving target hardness.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The flattening proof only refutes sources that expose or imply low-exponent semantic covers. It does not construct a row with no such cover.
steps: Fix an accepted row T_m and a depth-d semantic cover tree with d=2^{o(m)}.
Hardwire every node summary from every level into a nonuniform circuit; the total hardwired information at level i is at most 2^{(a_i+mu_i+o(1))m}.
On input x in {0,1}^m, compute the rank/path of the relevant node at each level using the declared ranker or charge this cost to the opener.
Compose the shared openers along the path and use multiplexers to retrieve the appropriate summaries; multiplexer overhead is polynomial in m times the total summary length.
The resulting circuit size is bounded by the maximum over summary mass exponents and opener exponents, giving CC(T_m)<=2^{(alpha_tree+o(1))m}.
If the source asserted CC(T_m)>2^{theta m} with alpha_tree<theta, the asserted MCSP no-side soundness is contradicted, so the cover is a valid route-level falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: Absence of all semantic covers below theta is equivalent to an unrestricted circuit lower bound for the row. A source theorem must provide a nonnatural, advice-free, searchable anti-ball certificate rather than merely rename the lower bound.

assumptions: Model is unrestricted fan-in two Boolean circuits; nonuniform hardwiring of all summaries is allowed in the MCSP lower-bound audit.
Tree depth is d(m)<=2^{o(m)}, and path navigation, node ranking, and boundary decoding have size 2^{o(m)} or are charged to the relevant opener.
The proposed carrier claims a constant threshold theta>0 for infinitely many or kappa-dense source lengths, not merely average-case or uniform hardness.
The cover is semantic: summaries need only exist and be nonuniformly hardwired; they need not be generated by the original verifier.
definitions: source object: an advice-free generated MCSP anti-ball carrier row T_m in {0,1}^{2^m}, optionally accompanied by a generated proof stream P_m.
target object: an E-language L_T whose padded length blocks are obtained from the carrier rows and whose desired consequence is an unrestricted circuit lower bound.
controlled interface: a semantic cover tree consisting of rankable block/node summaries and shared opener circuits that recover row bits from summaries.

target-preserving condition: kappa-dense source lengths, low distinct-image entropy D, and E-uniform row generation must remain intact; a subthreshold cover exponent refutes the source before any transfer.
CC(T_m) denotes unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size for the length-m truth table.
a_i is the exponent of the number of rankable nodes at tree level i; mu_i is the summary-length exponent; omega_i is the shared opener-size exponent.

equations.label: tree_cover_exponent
equations.valid_when: Valid when a semantic cover tree has subexponential depth, rankable nodes, and all navigation costs are either subexponential or charged to the opener.

equations.label: flattened_circuit_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after hardwiring every level summary and composing the shared openers along a single input path in the unrestricted nonuniform circuit model.

equations.label: soundness_necessary_condition
equations.valid_when: Requires the source row to be claimed as an MCSP no-instance above threshold 2^{theta m} on the same length m.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If no rankable node set and no shared opener can be extracted, the lemma gives no falsifier; if alpha_tree>=theta, the source survives only this audit and still needs a genuine anti-ball certificate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific no-go and validation upgrade: recursive summaries, Merkle-like openings, and multilevel proof streams cannot evade the semantic-cover leakage audit.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Hierarchical semantic-cover flattening. Let T_m be an accepted truth-table row claimed to satisfy CC(T_m)>2^{theta m}. Suppose T_m has a depth d=2^{o(m)} semantic cover tree: level i has at most 2^{a_i m+o(m)} rankable nodes, each node summary has length 2^{mu_i m+o(m)}, and the shared opener at level i has unrestricted circuit size 2^{omega_i m+o(m)}. Then T_m has an unrestricted circuit of size 2^{(alpha_tree+o(1))m}, where alpha_tree=max_i{a_i+mu_i,omega_i}. Thus any proposed MCSP no-side carrier with alpha_tree<theta is invalid; this is a finite falsifier for recursive-summary proof streams.

assumptions: Universal-circuit evaluation overhead is 2^{o(m)} relative to a 2^{alpha m} circuit description.
The cover summary may contain arbitrary nonuniform information about T_m, matching the unrestricted circuit model.
The comparison is row-wise and does not by itself give E-uniform locatability or density.
definitions: source object: a single truth table T_m of length 2^m proposed as an MCSP hard row.
target object: an unrestricted circuit lower bound CC(T_m)>2^{theta m} used by the carrier transfer.
bridge observable: existence or nonexistence of semantic covers below a stated exponent.
non-claim boundary: cover absence is a lower-bound restatement, not an independent proof of P != NP.

equations.label: circuit_to_cover
equations.valid_when: Valid when the cover is allowed to store a circuit description as its single semantic summary.

equations.label: cover_to_circuit
equations.valid_when: Applies when the cover summaries are rankable and the opener is an unrestricted circuit with the declared exponent.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the source restricts covers to efficiently generated summaries only, the converse can fail; the MCSP audit must use semantic nonuniform covers.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents overclaiming: the semantic-cover gate is a falsifier normal form, not a standalone construction of hard rows.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Flat-cover equivalence boundary. A truth table T_m has CC(T_m)<=2^{alpha m} iff, up to o(1) exponents, it has a one-node semantic cover whose summary is a circuit for T_m and whose opener is universal circuit evaluation. Conversely any semantic cover of exponent alpha gives a circuit of exponent alpha+o(1). Therefore proving absence of all covers below theta is not an easier source invariant; it is a normal form for the same unrestricted lower bound.

assumptions: For every large target length, a source length lies within the declared kappa gap after image-index multiplexing.
The unranking of distinct emitted images costs 2^{O(m)} time and does not use nonuniform selectors.
The row-hardness threshold theta is below every known implementation cap, including checkpoint, opener, and semantic-cover caps.
The conclusion is a conditional circuit lower bound for the constructed E language, not a proof of P != NP.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: a kappa-dense sequence of generated MCSP carrier rows with bounded distinct-image entropy D.
target object: a padded E language formed by canonical image-index multiplexing over the carrier rows.
bridge observable: row hardness certified by absence of subtheta semantic tree covers.
target-preserving condition: generation, unranking, and padding use no advice and keep the target inside E.

equations.label: multiplexed_length
equations.valid_when: Valid when the image-index multiplexing uses Dm+o(m) selector bits and the padding gap is bounded by kappa.

equations.label: extracted_exponent
equations.valid_when: Applies after row hardness 2^{theta m} survives the semantic-cover audit and the E-uniform multiplexing map preserves lengths.

equations.label: contradiction_transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires the target circuit for the multiplexed language to induce a circuit for the selected hard row without advice loss.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Fails if hard-row selection uses advice, if D is unbounded, if generation is outside E, or if any semantic tree cover has exponent below theta.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Maintains the established carrier-to-E transfer with the new prerequisite that hierarchical semantic covers are absent below theta.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Conditional low-D transfer after cover audit. Suppose kappa-dense source lengths carry E-uniformly generated rows, the distinct-image entropy is D, canonical unranking is in E, and at least one extracted row per source length has no semantic tree cover below theta. Then the multiplexed padded E language has unrestricted circuit lower bound exponent every delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)). This remains route-level progress only and is valid only after the tree-cover falsifier has not fired.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine this source family if every plausible generator yields a semantic tree cover with alpha_tree<theta or needs advice for hard-row selection.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a named source gives kappa-dense, low-D, E-uniform rows and proves no semantic tree cover below theta without invoking nonuniform hardness as an oracle.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a stronger route-specific disqualifier for generated MCSP carriers and a clearer boundary separating validation progress from a proof of P != NP.

dependency_updates.description: Generalizes block-summary leakage to recursive and hierarchical summaries; any subtheta flattened exponent refutes MCSP no-side soundness.
No-cover below theta is equivalent to unrestricted row lower bound up to o(1), so it is a falsifier normal form rather than an independent source theorem.
The delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) transfer remains valid only after the semantic tree-cover cap is cleared.
Need a sparse generated nonnatural anti-ball certificate with high semantic covering dimension, no advice, and no subthreshold opener.

falsifiers: A hierarchical semantic cover with alpha_tree<theta is a finite falsifier for the claimed MCSP no-side carrier.
A compressed proof skeleton with indexed row opening exponent omega<theta gives a nonuniform circuit for each row.
A checkpoint or block-summary implementation with max{1-lambda+mu,omega}<theta invalidates the source even if the generator is sequential.
An algebraically skippable transition, such as affine, LFSR, or iteratable proof generation, yields a row opener and defeats MCSP soundness.
A nonuniform hard-row selector or advice-dependent image unranking breaks the target-preserving transfer to an E language.
A dense polytime-decidable projection that excludes all small circuits becomes a natural-property falsifier unless sparsity or proof-mediated nonconstructivity is preserved.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: If min_lambda max{1-lambda+mu(lambda),omega(lambda)}<theta, the proposed generator is invalid. If every value is at least theta, the source survives this cover audit but still has not proved row hardness.
held_fixed_controls: Claimed row threshold theta for CC(T_m)>2^{theta m}.
Advice-free E-time sequential generation of the row/proof stream.
Distinct-image entropy D and kappa-density of source lengths.
Unrestricted nonuniform circuits as the MCSP target model.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Design now as a falsifier probe.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs to know whether recursive proof streams genuinely evade one-level semantic covers or only hide a lower-exponent cover in their block summaries.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, imagine a generated anti-ball carrier G_m that emits a row T_m and a long proof stream; every interval of 2^{lambda m} row/proof positions has a deterministic digest of length 2^{mu(lambda)m} and a shared opener O_lambda of size 2^{omega(lambda)m}.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal extraction of rankable summaries and openers from the generator for the negative case, or a proof that no semantic tree cover below theta exists plus E-canonical low-D unranking for the positive transfer.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: lambda, the block-size exponent in the semantic cover tree.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 72 upgrades the semantic-cover audit from one-level summaries to hierarchical proof streams. Recursive summaries flatten to unrestricted circuits with exponent max_i{a_i+mu_i,omega_i}; hence Merkle-like, checkpoint, or digest-based repairs are invalid whenever this exponent is below theta. The useful contribution is a sharper falsifier gate, while the positive source theorem remains open and equivalent to proving genuine row hardness by nonnatural means.
